text:
maria (Support): Hey team — customer reported 401 invalid_api_key when calling /v1/generate. They pasted curl and response here. Says it started after a deploy but might be key-related. Repro attached.

maria (Support): Customer's curl (redacted key):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H \"Authorization: \"Bearer \"sk_OLDKEY12345\"\" \n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \n  -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-1\", \"input\":\"hi\"}'
```

maria (Support): Response: 401, body: `\{\"error\":\{\"type\":\"invalid_api_key\",\"message\":\"Invalid or expired API key\"\}\}`. Customer says they haven't rotated keys recently.

devin (Eng API): Thanks — quick checks: 1) did they include extra quotes around the header? The curl shows nested quotes, looks suspicious. 2) which header are they using (Authorization vs x-api-key)? 3) any proxies or env var templating that might add whitespace?

maria (Support): They said they copy/pasted from their env var into a startup script. Might be a shell quoting issue. Asked for full request headers but customer provided only curl.

sre-ops: I pulled the request from ingress logs by IP/time. Correlation id 4f2a1b. Log shows auth failure from token id tk_8f... status=401 reason=key_expired. Cross-checking key registry now.

api-bot: key-status: tk_8fXXXXXXXX - expires 2026-02-20T03:14:10Z - state: expired :lock: (queried by sre-ops)

devin (Eng API): OK that matches expired key. Two common gotchas to share with customer: 1) some SDKs cache keys in memory so redeploy/ restart after rotating; 2) trailing newline/leading whitespace or extra quotes will cause the server to reject as malformed. Show them correct curl.

clarice (DevEx): Pasting a minimal repro they can run to prove header formatting:
```
# correct (no extra quotes)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_NEWKEY12345" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"are you there?"}'

# common bad example that causes 401
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H \"Authorization: \"Bearer sk_NEWKEY12345\"\" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"are you there?"}'
```

maria (Support): I told the customer to check the key in their dashboard and rotate if expired, and to retry with the correct curl. Also asked them to search their repo for any hardcoded old keys.

customer (via maria): Reported they found an old key in a Kubernetes secret that hadn't been updated after a credential rotation. They rotated the key and updated the secret, restarted pods.

sre-ops: Verified incoming requests after their restart — new key id tk_a1bcdef accepted, status 200, sample log: `{correlation:4f2a1b, route:/v1/generate, status:200, key_id:tk_a1bcdef}`

maria (Support): Customer confirms success, no more 401s. Closing loop and leaving notes: - cause: expired key + one instance still using old secret - action: rotated key, updated k8s secret, restarted workload - customer lesson: rotate and update env/secrets, watch for cached SDK processes.

devin (Eng API): Recommend adding one-off webhook or dashboard flag to warn when a service account has active tokens expiring within X days. Filing a small ticket for product: PF-392 (optional).

clarice (DevEx): I'll update the docs section "Auth: common 401 causes" to explicitly show the bad-quote example and mention trailing newline.

maria (Support): Thanks all. Marking thread resolved. :white_check_mark:
